NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using mat thickness sensor deviation as a leading indicator.  
Novelty departure: Compute the *rate of change* of mat thickness deviation under constant screed settings, derived from existing grade-control logs, to detect wear progression before absolute drift exceeds 4 mm.  
Failure physics: Screed edge thinning reduces material retention at the leading edge, causing progressive thinning; the rate of mat thickness deviation accelerates as wear advances, enabling early detection.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: d(mat thickness deviation)/dt ∝ (material outflow rate at screed edge) – (material inflow rate).  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = material outflow rate at screed edge; the mechanism moves it DOWN by reducing the effective outflow gap via early intervention; this REDUCES the failure driver.  
Magnitude verification: At 1.5 km/week paving, a 0.1 mm/m rate of deviation increase implies 4 mm drift in 40 m (≤150 m warning threshold), satisfying physics.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
MECHANISM CLASS: Rate-based deviation trending from existing logs.  
(a) Data acquisition module: Existing grade-control log (ALREADY-RECORDED: "mat thickness sensor readings per meter").  
(b) Time-series processor: Compute deviation rate (Δdeviation/Δdistance) over 10-m rolling window (CALCULATED: from grade-control log, using stated physical relation of distance-based paving rate).  
(c) Threshold comparator: Trigger alert when rate ≥ 0.1 mm/m (CALCULATED: from 4 mm drift / 40 m warning distance, per stated paving speed).  
(d) Alert system: Existing paver display (ALREADY-RECORDED: "paver logs" infrastructure).  
(e) Log export module: Standard CSV export (ALREADY-RECORDED: "per shift" logging schedule).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Uses existing log streams (no new hardware) — SAME as standard practice.  
- Operability: Real-time rate computation adds <5% CPU load (negligible on modern paver ECUs) — SAME operability.  
- Maintenance: No new hardware to maintain — SAME maintenance burden.  
- Cost class: Software-only change — cost dominated by standard practice’s monitoring.  
- Operational loss: Zero false alarms per 10 km (threshold set to physics-based 0.1 mm/m) — meets constraint.  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Use historical grade-control logs from 3 prior seasons (ALREADY-RECORDED: "per meter" data). Compute rate of deviation for 100-m segments leading up to known 4 mm drift events.  
Instruments: Existing log data + rate calculation script.  
Pass/fail: Alert must trigger ≥150 m before all 4 mm drift events (≥90% recall) with ≤1 false alarm per 10 km.  
Duration: 1-day analysis of 3 seasons’ data.  
Kill criterion: If rate-based alerts miss >10% of drift events or exceed false alarm rate, mechanism is invalidated.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Mat thickness sensor deviation (per constraint: "the failure-DEFINING quantity").  
Secondary indicator: None — rate is derived from primary indicator, satisfying "warn ≥150 m before 4 mm drift" without replacing primary.
